llm.label: LLM (Large Language Model)
llm.def: A model trained on huge amounts of text that predicts the next piece of text. Chat, code, summaries: everything starts from there.

token.label: Token
token.def: The piece of text a model works with: a word, part of a word or a symbol. Qwen3 knows about 150,000 of them.

weights.label: Weights (parameters)
weights.def: The numbers stored in the model, from millions to billions. Training a model means adjusting these numbers.

training.label: Training
training.def: Showing examples to the model, measuring its error, and adjusting its weights so it gets a bit less wrong. In a loop.

pretraining.label: Pre-training
pretraining.def: The first training: predicting the continuation of trillions of tokens. Months of GPU time, done by labs (Alibaba, Meta, Google…).

continuedpretraining.label: Continued pre-training
continuedpretraining.def: Resuming the pre-training objective (predicting the next token) on raw, unlabeled text from a specific domain (code, medicine, law…), to teach the model its vocabulary and knowledge. No question/answer pairs: just text.

posttraining.label: Post-training
posttraining.def: Any training done after pre-training to steer the model: a format, a tone, a task, a domain.

base.label: Base model (foundation)
base.def: A model fresh out of pre-training: it completes text, but can't answer a question or follow an instruction.

instruct.label: Instruct model (it, chat)
instruct.def: A base model already post-trained to follow instructions and answer like an assistant.

openweight.label: Open-weight
openweight.def: A model whose weights are published, under a license that allows reusing and modifying them.

frontier.label: Frontier model
frontier.def: The biggest models of the moment (Claude, GPT, Gemini…), served through an API. Great at everything, but expensive, remote and closed.

finetuning.label: Fine-tuning
finetuning.def: Continuing the training of an existing model on your own data. "Full fine-tuning" updates every weight.

lora.label: LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation)
lora.def: The original weights are frozen and only two small matrices added next to them are trained. 5 to 8 times less memory, ~95% of the effectiveness.

rank.label: Rank (LoRA)
rank.def: The inner size of the two small LoRA matrices: B is (d × r) and A is (r × d), so r sets how many weights are trained. A higher rank lets the adapter learn more, but costs more memory. Common values: 8 to 64.

adapter.label: Adapter
adapter.def: The output of a LoRA training: a small file (a few dozen MB) applied on top of the original model, or merged into it.

sft.label: SFT (Supervised Fine-Tuning)
sft.def: Learning by imitation: the model is shown "input → correct answer" pairs and learns to reproduce the answer.

loss.label: Loss
loss.def: How much probability the model gave to the correct token: 90% means a near-zero loss, 1% a big one. It's the model's "surprise" at the right answer, and training drives it down.

gradient.label: Gradient
gradient.def: For each weight, the direction and size of the change that lowers the loss. "Gradient descent" follows that direction.

backprop.label: Backpropagation
backprop.def: The algorithm that sends the error back from the output to the input, layer by layer, to compute every weight's gradient in one pass.

learningrate.label: Learning rate
learningrate.def: The step size: how far each weight moves in the direction of the gradient. Too big and training diverges; too small and it doesn't progress.

epoch.label: Epoch
epoch.def: One full pass over the whole training dataset. Two epochs: every example is seen twice.

batch.label: Batch
batch.def: A group of examples processed together: their errors are averaged before updating the weights. More stable than one example at a time.

hyperparams.label: Hyperparameters
hyperparams.def: The settings we choose (LoRA rank, learning rate, batch size, epochs…), as opposed to the weights, which the model learns.

distillation.label: Distillation
distillation.def: Training a small model (the student) on the answers of a big model (the teacher).

teacher.label: Teacher model
teacher.def: The big model that writes the training examples. Here DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, through OpenRouter.

heldout.label: Held-out set
heldout.def: A part of the dataset set aside and never shown during training. Same mold as the training set: it measures what the model learned.

benchmark.label: Benchmark
benchmark.def: A frozen evaluation set, written by a different source than the training data. It's the exam that counts.

overfitting.label: Overfitting
overfitting.def: The model recites its examples instead of generalizing: excellent on what it has seen, worse on everything else.

fewshot.label: Few-shot
fewshot.def: Putting a few solved examples in the prompt, without training anything. Zero-shot: no examples at all.

chattemplate.label: Chat template
chattemplate.def: The exact format (tags, system, user and assistant roles) in which an instruct model expects its conversations.

dpo.label: DPO (Direct Preference Optimization)
dpo.def: Learning from preferences: for the same input, one preferred answer and one rejected. The model learns to lean towards the first.

kto.label: KTO
kto.def: A DPO variant: each answer is simply labeled good or bad, no pairs needed.

rlhf.label: RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback)
rlhf.def: The model generates, a judge (trained on human ratings) scores, and the model reinforces what scores well. RLAIF: the judge is an AI.

grpo.label: GRPO
grpo.def: Reinforcement without a learned judge: several answers per question, scored by a verifiable rule, compared to the group average.

rft.label: RFT (Rejection sampling Fine-Tuning)
rft.def: The model generates several answers, the correct ones are kept, and an SFT is run on them.

rag.label: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)
rag.def: Finding relevant documents and giving them to the model in the prompt. For knowledge that changes, rather than training.

inference.label: Inference
inference.def: Using the model to generate an answer, as opposed to training it.

quantization.label: Quantization
quantization.def: Storing weights on fewer bits (16 → 4): a model 3 to 4 times lighter, for a small loss in quality.

mlx.label: MLX
mlx.def: Apple's machine learning framework, a PyTorch equivalent optimized for Apple Silicon chips.

onnx.label: ONNX
onnx.def: A standard model export format, readable by many runtimes, including Transformers.js in the browser.

transformersjs.label: Transformers.js
transformersjs.def: Hugging Face's JS library for running models in the browser, on WebGPU or WebAssembly.

webgpu.label: WebGPU
webgpu.def: The browser API that gives access to the machine's GPU, for rendering or compute.
